correctness.rationale: For every m>=1 and lambda>mu>0 the two-plane rank-one Schur determinant yields exact eigenvalues 1, K(t), and m-1 copies of h2. The strict derivative and cross-multiplication yield impossibility and exact threshold. Independent Gaussian squares yield the regularized beta tail. Chi-square LLN with lambda scaling proves the two separate critical windows and all boundary 0/1 statements. The actual companion Python checks 1,108 finite cases and examples but is not proof of infinite limits.

originality.rationale: The same Gaussian covariance A+A² and Nyström spectral LMP are defined in the inspected source; the new claim is strictly the exact one-probe condition-number improvement event, threshold obstruction, beta success distribution and two critical exponents, not the original algorithm. Frangella–Tropp–Udell analyze a scaled preconditioner and effective-dimension/expected-conditioning bound, not the unscaled rank-one event; other inspected work addresses deterministic perturbations or random Nyström approximation errors. Published semantic result queries yield nearby but implication-distinct facts. Residual risk is equivalent treatment in older specialized or differently named preconditioner literature.
residual_risks: An equivalent beta-law may have been published under a different preconditioner parameterization or in nonindexed sources.
The entire Frangella manuscript and the Persson/Boullé/Kressner open-access manuscript were not verified exhaustively at the theorem/appendix level.
Database similarity retrieval alone cannot establish novelty; exact mathematical comparisons and primary sources are the main evidence.

value.rationale: A recent EDA method claims practical merit from using inexpensive covariance A+A² rather than a sequential power sketch. The theorem supplies a precise spectral-condition-number improvement probability, exposes an all-sketch no-improvement boundary at h1<=h2², and proves genuinely different m^1/4 and m^1/2 success scales. These are nontrivial finite-sample and asymptotic calibration benchmarks. Since the model has two eigenvalues, it does not prove CG iteration savings; this limitation is explicitly stated.
